title: Fix a stale state in setInterval with an updater
summary: A counter that stops at 1, a dependency that should not be there, and a step prop that should.

turns.user: Ticker gets to 1 and stops. the interval is still firing afaict

assistant.body: The effect runs once, on the first render, so the callback it created still sees count as 0. It writes 0 + 1 every second, which is why the screen sits at 1. Adding count to the dependency array rebuilds the callback with the latest value.

turns.user: ok it counts now. but isnt that tearing down the interval every single tick

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was not the right fix. With count in the array, every tick runs clearInterval and setInterval again. Pass setCount a function instead and React hands it the latest value. The effect stops reading count, so the array can go back to empty.

turns.user: oh and the increment should come from props. step or something

assistant.body: Here's the step version. This time the effect does read step, so step belongs in the array, and the interval is rebuilt only when step changes.
sed -i '' -e 's/export function Ticker() {/export function Ticker({ step }: { step: number }) {/' -e 's/c + 1/c + step/' -e 's/}, \[\])/}, [step])/' src/components/Ticker.tsx
